name: selfboost
description: Audit your MCP server's tools and measure how often AI agents pick it. List the servers in your selfboo.st workspace with their audit and Pick Scores, read an audit's failing checks, fixes and suggested tool rewrites, audit a server again after you change it, and run pick tests: simulations that ask AI models which connector they would suggest for your prompts, against your competitors, with a 90% interval. selfboo.st reads a server's tools with initialize and tools/list only; it never calls them.

interface.shortDescription: Audit and test your MCP server
interface.longDescription:
selfboo.st helps the people who build MCP servers see how AI agents choose between servers, and why theirs is passed over. Connected to ChatGPT, it works with the servers in your selfboo.st workspace, so you can check and improve your tools from a conversation.

What you can do:
- List the MCP servers in your workspace with their tool counts, latest audit score and latest Pick Score.
- Read a server's audit: a 0–100 score across five dimensions, every failing check with its fix, and a suggested rewrite of each tool's title, description and parameters.
- Fetch a server's tools again after you change them, and audit them again.
- See the intents a server is tested on (the jobs it should win) with their prompts and competitors.
- Start a pick test and read its result: how often AI models choose your server over its competitors for your prompts, with a 90% interval, by model, by intent and by competitor.

Good to know:
- Pick tests are simulations. They ask AI models, through their APIs, which connector they would suggest when shown your listing and your competitors'. They are not ChatGPT's or any other app's real ranking, and every score names the models it ran on.
- selfboo.st reads a server's tools by sending it initialize and tools/list only. It never calls a server's tools and never changes your server: it suggests, and you decide what to ship.
- Servers, intents, prompts and competitors are added in the selfboo.st app; from ChatGPT you read and test them.
- You need a selfboo.st account.
capabilities: List your MCP servers with their audit and Pick Scores
Read an audit: failing checks, fixes and suggested tool rewrites
Fetch a server's tools again and re-audit them
List the intents, prompts and competitors a server is tested on
Run a pick test against your competitors
Read pick-test results by model, intent and competitor
defaultPrompt: Which of my MCP servers has the lowest audit score, and why?
How should I rewrite my server's tool descriptions so agents pick it?
How often do AI models pick my server over its competitors?

positive.description: List the servers in the workspace with their scores.
positive.prompt: Which MCP servers are in my selfboo.st workspace, and how do they score?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_servers and lists every server in the test workspace with its name, address, tool count, latest audit score and latest Pick Score. It changes nothing.

positive.description: Explain why agents pass over a server, from its latest audit.
positive.prompt: Why would AI agents pass over my MCP server? Show me its latest audit and what to fix first.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the server with list_servers, then calls get_audit and reports the 0–100 score, the five dimension scores, the most severe failing checks with their fixes, and the suggested rewrite for at least one tool. Nothing is changed on the server.

positive.description: Audit a server again after its tools changed.
positive.prompt: I just changed my MCP server's tool descriptions. Fetch its tools again and audit it.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls run_audit for the server, says the new audit takes about thirty seconds and uses a few credits, then reads the result with get_audit and reports the new score. It reads the server's tools with tools/list only and never calls them.

positive.description: List the intents a server is tested on.
positive.prompt: Which intents is my MCP server tested on, and how many prompts and competitors does each have?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_intents for the server and lists each intent with its prompt count, competitor count and last Pick Score. It changes nothing.

positive.description: Run a pick test and read its result as a simulation.
positive.prompt: Run a pick test on my MCP server and tell me how often the models chose it over its competitors.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls run_pick_test, reports the test id, the models it runs on and the credits it uses, then calls get_pick_test. While the test runs it reports its progress; once done it gives the Pick Score with its 90% interval, the score by model and by intent and each competitor's share, and says the result is a simulation on the named models, not ChatGPT's real ranking.

negative.description: selfboo.st never calls a server's tools, so a request to run a tool on the user's server must not be carried out through it; the assistant should say selfboo.st only reads tool definitions.
negative.prompt: Call the get_weather tool on my MCP server with city set to Paris.

negative.description: selfboo.st suggests rewrites but cannot edit or deploy a server, so a request to change and ship the server must not be carried out through it; the assistant can offer the suggested rewrites instead.
negative.prompt: Rewrite my MCP server's tool descriptions and deploy the change to production.

negative.description: An everyday request unrelated to MCP servers must not trigger selfboo.st.
negative.prompt: Book a table for two at a seafood restaurant in Istanbul tonight.

review.commerce_description: selfboo.st sells nothing inside ChatGPT or Codex, and the plugin processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release. Connect your selfboo.st workspace: list your MCP servers with their audit and Pick Scores, read an audit's failing checks, fixes and suggested tool rewrites, audit a server again after you change it, and run and read pick tests, simulations of how often AI models choose your server over its competitors, each naming the models it ran on.
